name: 1720 Prairie Avenue — Tyrrell/Walker Italianate frame, K16 clapboard

grade.why: Pictured: 2 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 24.000, v -0.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation -0.581 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1720 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1720 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '2BB' printed on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys, which the photograph shows over a raised basement, the porch floor and the front door about 1.55 m over the walk.

construction.note: Drawn yellow, the sheet's colour for frame; the photograph shows the front in clapboard with corner boards. Built board by board from the K16 timber kit at a frame wall's 0.15 m.

frame_house.note: The whole house from the K16 kit (T-3180, piece 1 of T-1873), refined from the district draft in place. READ from the 1911 sheet through the T-2328 trace s20fp-1720-b1 and the draft's fit of it: the main block's rectangle (22.25 m deep, 10 m along Prairie), the two-storey south wing (u 10-21.5, standing 0.75 m back from the front) and the one-storey range across the front, here the porch, 1.5 m deep. READ from the Tyrrell photograph through its camera (data/reference_views/walker_house_1720_prairie/tyrrell_front.json), at about 80 px a metre on the front: the porch floor and the door 1.55 m over the walk (a 1.4 m foundation under the clapboard, the porch floor raised 0.95 m over the kit's), the frieze about 1.1 m deep under the eave at about 10.2 m, the upper sash between about 6.4 and 8.4 m and the lower between 2.2 and 4.5 m; the front's openings where the photograph puts them, measured from the south corner: below, a single round-headed light at 2.0 m, the door at 4.8 m, a pair at 8.0 m; above, single round-headed sash at 2.5 and 5.0 m and a pair at 7.9 m; the porch across the front from about v -1.35 to 9.55 m (the sheet's range runs -2.0 to 8.25; the photograph is preferred where it shows the porch reaching nearly to the north corner; T-3181 measured its 925 px at the porch's own depth, about 85 px a metre, where T-3180 had used the wall's 80), centred on its stair at 4.1 m. T-3181 (piece 2 of T-1873) READ from the same photograph, at the porch's depth: the posts paired, 0.26 m between centres, at its ends and either side of its middle opening, 1.3 m out (x 65-100, 385-430, 610-655 and 928-980 px); the plate's underside at y 518 px, about 3.9 m over the floor, under a fascia 0.13 m deep to the deck at about y 482; a segmental arch over each opening, springing at about y 556 px (0.45 m under the plate) and crowned at y 538 over the side openings and 543 over the middle (rises of 0.21 and 0.15 m); a turned balustrade 0.7 m high (top rail y 800, bottom rail y 855) in each side opening, about sixteen balusters to a side (0.21 m apart); the stair as broad as the middle opening (2.24 m, its cheeks rising to the inner posts), each side a raking balustrade on a closed string; and iron cresting about 0.5 m high on the deck (y 437-482 px) with posts about 0.37 m apart. RECONSTRUCTED and recorded as L-k16-1720-frame-house-3180: every opening on the flanks, the wing and the rear; the kit's two-over-two sash there and the kit's sash and casings on the front (the photograph's arched casings and hoods are T-3182's); the hip's 20-degree pitch; the one brick stack (the draft rules gave two; the photograph shows two stacks over the roof, the second not built); the paint. RECONSTRUCTED by T-3181 and recorded under the same liberty: the balusters' vase profile, the kit's chamfered posts for the print's turned ones, the cresting's cast panels as plain bars between knobbed posts and its return along the porch roof's north end, and newels where the print's stair rails end in scrolls. NOT YET BUILT, owned by T-3182, the last piece of T-1873: the upper storey's canted bay, the arched casings and hoods, the frieze's attic lights, the paired brackets and the central front gable (T-3182).

roof_covering.note: No roof covering has been read for 1720: the photograph sees only the eave of a low hip. A low-pitched Italianate hip of the late 1860s was commonly covered in painted tin; its dark grey is reconstructed.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2BB frame (yellow) dwelling (D) with a bay'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-3180 (piece 1 of T-1873) refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id: the whole house is rebuilt from the K16 timber kit as clapboard walls, cased sash, a bracketed eave under a low hip, a two-storey south wing and a porch across the front, read from the 1911 Sanborn sheet 20 and from the undated Tyrrell photograph (glessner_blog_1720_tyrrell_photo), whose camera is solved at data/reference_views/walker_house_1720_prairie/tyrrell_front.json. Otis L. Wheelock designed the house for John Tyrrell in 1868 (glessner_blog_2022_01_burley_tyrrell). The photograph's porch detail is T-3181's and its upper storey, bay and central gable T-3182's; until they land the match record says what still differs. Liberty L-k16-1720-frame-house-3180.
